claims.text: The initial material is an additively manufactured, dual-nanoprecipitation Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has a baseline nanoscale distribution of Ti, Cr, and other alloying elements.
During high-temperature oxidation, the dual nanoprecipitates undergo dynamic elemental redistribution.
Elemental redistribution in the nanoprecipitates facilitates formation of a protective oxide layer.
In situ high-resolution TEM with concurrent EDS/EELS mapping can examine nanoscale morphology and elemental redistribution during oxidation in real time.
Controlled oxygen partial pressure and temperature ramps can replicate gas-turbine or aerospace service oxidation conditions.
Oxygen ingress causes preferential oxidation of selected alloying elements within the nanoprecipitates.
Preferential oxidation drives enrichment or depletion of Ti, Cr, or Al at nanoprecipitate–matrix interfaces.
Interfacial compositional shifts promote development of a continuous protective oxide layer.
Time-resolved TEM and EDS/EELS will reveal changes in nanoprecipitate morphology and elemental distribution correlated with oxide formation and growth at nanoprecipitate interfaces.
The resulting protective oxide is expected to mitigate further oxidation degradation.
Ex situ post-oxidation analyses provide static snapshots of oxide layers and nanoprecipitates.
Ex situ analyses may miss dynamic elemental-redistribution processes.
The proposed dynamic effects are significant only during high-temperature oxidation under controlled oxygen partial pressures.
At lower temperatures or non-representative conditions, elemental redistribution may be minimal or undetectable.
The kinetics and extent of elemental redistribution are uncertain because oxidation kinetics interact with nanoprecipitate stability.
Variations in local chemistry may influence whether the oxide layer is protective.
